Walking Intervention — Pre/Post
⚠ DATA CORRECTION (2026-09-26, re-run complete)
Six sessions had duplicated / mixed-up BIDS data (sub-034/065/074/084/091 ses-02, sub-089 ses-01); two further subjects (sub-056, sub-057) are excluded pending archive re-acquisition. FastSurfer / fMRIPrep / XCP-D and all FC/EC features and statistics were re-run on the corrected data (an earlier re-extraction attempt had silently failed; it was re-run and verified before this report). Headline changes: the subcortical-volume finding is NULL (0 FDR-significant; the previously reported 7 were an artifact); the EC picture is now limbic → cerebellum (replicated across all five EC methods and every cerebellum parcellation, including the new DiFuMo-512 whole-brain representation); FC Motor_L whole-brain remains the top seed effect; structural connectivity is complete (106/106 sessions).

Walking Intervention vs Control — Multimodal Results

Preliminary · 53 structural subjects (105 sessions) / 44 FC-EC subjects (85 obs) / ~39 voxelwise · all group×time interactions · FDR or cluster-corrected · effective connectivity via rDCM/VAR/Granger/K-SG TE · cerebellum parcellations from coarse to fine (single node / zones / Buckner-7 / DiFuMo-512 whole-brain, primary)

Headline (corrected 2026-09-26, re-run complete): after fixing 6 sessions with duplicated/mixed-up BIDS data, the subcortical-volume finding is null (0 FDR-significant structures). Cortical thickness is unchanged. The surviving signals are functional/effective-connectivity: reduced Motor_L whole-brain coupling in walkers (seed-to-brain; Seed-to-Brain tab) and a limbic → cerebellum directed effect that replicates across all five EC methods and every cerebellum parcellation, including the new whole-brain DiFuMo-512 representation (this revision). Structural connectivity (106/106 sessions) shows a small set of cerebellum–attention/default effects and no limbic→cerebellum edge, as expected for anatomy vs dynamics.

Interpretation

No structural effect survives correction. After excluding the duplicated/mixed-up sessions, none of the 10 subcortical structures, DKT regions, or cortical-thickness maps shows a group×time interaction (top trend Right-Thalamus q=0.15). Two readings: (i) a short walking intervention is unlikely to change gross subcortical volume — structural change on this timescale is biologically implausible — so the null is the expected result; (ii) the study is only powered for large effects (n=53, 105 sessions). The functional/effective-connectivity effects reported in the ROI-to-ROI tab therefore carry the intervention signal, not macro-structure. The earlier "volume preservation" claim should not be cited.

Outlier screen

Two control subjects show large negative deltas: sub-063 (73F; L/R hippocampus −284/−257 mm³, z≈−3.6 both; its ICV also changed +7.2% between sessions, suggesting segmentation instability) and sub-077 (70F; left amygdala −232 mm³, z=−3.2). A third case, sub-067 (Walking), has mild bilateral MTL atrophy consistent with age. Refitting the LMM without sub-063+077 (n=51) or without all six flagged subjects (n=47) keeps 0 FDR-significant structures (top q=0.21 / 0.28), so the structural null does not depend on these subjects.

Subdivided ROIs (motor / hippocampus / cerebellum)

Finer parcellations (Glasser M1/S1/premotor, Tian hippocampal subfields, DiFuMo cerebellar components), re-run on corrected data (55 ROIs; 2 FDR-significant). The two significant ROIs are left cerebellar lobule VI superior (DiFuMo 161, q=0.019) and Crus I anterior (DiFuMo 172, q=0.021), both increasing in walkers relative to controls; lobule VI anterior (173) is a near-miss (q=0.054). Motor-cortex and hippocampal subdivisions are null — the cerebellar signal sits in the sensorimotor/learning cerebellum.

Full ROI-to-ROI (442×442) + NBS

No significant connected subnetworks (largest t=3.0 component 59 edges, p=0.93; t=2.5: 557 edges, p=0.94). The intervention's FC changes are diffuse — summary-level effects survive, coherent edge-clusters do not.

97,461 edges, delta (post−pre), two-sample t-test, Network-Based Statistic cluster correction (5,000 permutations).

Effective connectivity (EC)

Directed connectivity from the ec-variant denoised BOLD (0.01–0.1 Hz, 0 mm smoothing). The primary representation is the DiFuMo-512 whole-brain division: every block — cortical (Ctx-*), subcortical (Sub-*) and cerebellar (Cb-*) — is a voxel-level mean over DiFuMo-512 components grouped by derived Yeo-7 network. Sensitivity representations keep the 7 Yeo cortical networks + Subcortical fixed (442-parcel timeseries) and vary only the cerebellum: cerebellum as 1 node (9 nodes; 72 directed edges), functional zones (Motor/Cognitive/Vestibular; 11 nodes; 110 edges), Buckner-7 cerebellar networks (15 nodes; 210 edges), and the fine cerebellar DiFuMo-512 components (52 nodes; 2,652 edges). King-10 / MDTB-32 results are retained on disk for the publication stage and are not shown here. n=44 subjects (85 obs); LMM per edge ~ group×time + Age + Gender + mean_fd + (1|subject) with mean-FD > 0.3 mm excluded, BH-FDR within division×method. TR=0.8 s → HRF-latency confounded; hypothesis-generating, non-causal.

Network-to-network effect matrices (per map × method)

Directed group×time t for every representation — one figure per map, panels = method (rDCM / VAR(1) / pairwise Granger / binned TE / KSG-TE); rows = target, columns = source (same A[target, source] convention as rDCM/VAR); blue = negative, red = positive; * = FDR q<0.05. Node order within each figure follows that representation's node list. Full tables: ec/stats/matrices/ec_matrix_long.csv and ec_matrix_<method>_<map>.csv.

Reading the matrices: the negative (blue) block in the Limbic row / cerebellum columns in every map is the limbic→cerebellum effect; the red cells in the cerebellum rows / SomMot–DorsAttn–Cont columns are cerebellum→cortical effects. In the DiFuMo-512 whole-brain panel the same effect appears as Ctx-Limbic → Cb-* edges, i.e. with cortex, subcortex and cerebellum all in one atlas.

EC NBS (cluster-level, specification sweep)

NBS (Zalesky et al. 2010; 5,000 group-label permutations — the valid exchangeability scheme for the group×time interaction) was evaluated as a specification grid: primary threshold |t| ∈ {2.5, 2.75, 3.0, 3.5} × component statistic {extent, mass} × sign mode {unsigned, positive-only, negative-only}, on the primary DiFuMo-512 whole-brain division and on Buckner-7, for rDCM and VAR (96 specifications). Per-specification results: ec/stats/ec_nbs_sweep_*.csv.

Result: the whole-brain division is null under every specification (min p=0.34, rDCM and VAR). The only significant components are in the Buckner-7 division, for the negative-mass statistic (VAR: p=0.041 at |t|≥2.75, p=0.043 at 3.0) — and they are exactly the limbic→cerebellum edges (Limbic→Cb-SalVentAttn t=−3.6, Limbic→Cb-DorsAttn t=−3.2; at 2.75 also Vis→Limbic t=−3.0); rDCM shows the same component as a trend (p=0.056 at 3.0). With 96 specifications, this marginal cluster should be read as consistent with, not independent evidence for, the limbic→cerebellum finding. The conventional default (unsigned extent) is null everywhere, and NBS on the primary whole-brain division is null under all specifications.

Outlier screen (FC + EC + SC + DTI)

50 flagged subject×feature deltas (|z|>3 within group) among all significant features; refitting without flagged subjects changes 47 of 612 significant effects materially. The headline findings — Motor_L whole-brain (seed, corrected), limbic → cerebellum (EC), cerebellar SomMot axial kurtosis (DTI) — are unaffected; fragile effects are noted in the relevant sections (per-analysis detail in shared/outlier_flags.csv and outlier_robustness.csv).

Interpretation

Functional (ROI-to-ROI): the strongest between-network effect is Subcortical–Cerebellum (partial q=0.006), with several visual-network pairs; subdivided cerebellar lobules VI superior and Crus I anterior increase in walkers (q=0.019/0.021) with finer parcellations. Seed-based effects (Motor_L whole-brain q=0.003, DLPFC_L–Vis q=0.008, hippocampal networks) are reported in the Seed-to-Brain tab. Edge-level ROI-to-ROI NBS is null. Effective: the walking intervention is associated with a re-balancing of cerebellar communication — controls increased limbic→cerebellar influence (+0.037) while walkers decreased it (−0.020), whereas walkers increased cerebellar→sensorimotor (+0.039 vs −0.022) and cerebellar→dorsal-attention influence (+0.007 vs −0.038; all deltas post−pre). The limbic→cerebellum effect replicates in all five EC methods and every representation, including the DiFuMo-512 whole-brain blocks. FC changes are diffuse at the edge level (NBS null); cluster-level EC NBS is null on the whole-brain division under all 96 specifications, with only a marginal negative-mass cluster in the Buckner-7 division (VAR p≈0.04 — the limbic→cerebellum edges); EC at TR=0.8 s is HRF-latency confounded — hypothesis-generating.

Seed-to-Brain (seed metrics + seed-to-voxel)

Two families: (a) region-level seed metrics — seed→network and seed→whole-brain Fisher-z from the corrected FC metric tournament (n=44 subjects, 85 obs; LMM + BH-FDR); (b) voxelwise seed-to-voxel maps — per-subject delta (post−pre) images, FSL randomise TFCE (5,000 permutations), old cohort (pre-BIDS-correction), pending re-run on the corrected data.

Seed→whole-brain & seed→network metrics (corrected cohort)

Method note: these are not permutation tests. Each seed's coupling is a scalar summary of the 442×442 Fisher-z matrix — mean correlation with all other parcels (seed→whole-brain) or with the parcels of each target network (seed→network) — tested with the same LMM (group×time + Age + Gender + mean_fd) + BH-FDR as the ROI-to-ROI metrics. The permutation-based seed analyses are the voxelwise TFCE maps below (corrected-cohort re-run complete: null).

8 significant (q<0.05) of 180 seed tests (fc variant; 2 in the GSR robustness variant). Most robust: Motor_L → whole brain (partial, t=−3.52, q=0.003; walkers ↓ vs controls), DLPFC_L → Vis (partial, q=0.008), hippocampus → limbic/default/salience and Motor_L → SomMot pairs. Caveats: DLPFC_R → whole brain is fragile (q=0.045; weakens to 0.060 without sub-088), and seed effects are GSR-sensitive (top GSR q=0.078) unlike the ROI-to-ROI Subcortical–Cerebellum effect.

Voxelwise seed-to-voxel (corrected cohort, TFCE)

Ten seeds × two directions, 41 subjects (22 Control / 19 Walking), per-subject delta (post−pre) maps, FSL randomise TFCE, 5,000 permutations (script/extract_seed_voxel_maps.py + HPC array job 30309). Sensitivity: old parametric GRF model (same deltas, Welch + cluster)

The model behind the old reported seed maps — Welch t on subject deltas plus FSL GRF cluster correction (smoothest; z≥2.3, cluster p<0.05; script/group_lmm_stats.py) — reproduced exactly on the old data (LH-RN 6,359 significant voxels; RH-RN 6,214; HIP-head 10,826). Note this model has no per-subject EVs or random effects: one delta per subject (the app's subject-intercept mixed design in neuconn_app/utils/group_stats_design.py exists but was not used for these outputs). Applied to the corrected cohort (script/seed_welch_grf.py, validated), it finds hippocampus L (3 clusters; top 952 voxels, p=0.0011) and red nucleus R (1 cluster; 883 voxels, p=0.00014); the other eight seeds are null. Those two clusters do not survive the TFCE permutation run above, so the corrected voxelwise seed evidence is weak and method-dependent (and the corrected seed set uses the whole hippocampus, not the old head-subfield seed).

Microstructure effects: walkers show higher axial kurtosis in the cerebellar sensorimotor network (Buckner-7: Cb-SomMot q=0.009; King-10 Region7 Ak q=0.032) and lower MD in the salience/ventral-attention network (q=0.027), with planarity/linearity changes in cerebellar regions. FA itself only trends (Cb-SomMot q=0.054). The pattern — kurtosis up (more restricted/hindered diffusion) in cerebellar sensorimotor tissue and MD down in a cortical attention network — is consistent with the microstructural direction expected after aerobic training, but the effects are few (5/348) and DWI at 1.7 mm is modestly sensitive; hypothesis-generating. Note: MDTB-32/DiFuMo-512 are not in the DTI table (their atlases were not part of the QSIRecon run); adding them needs a per-subject atlas warp (feasible follow-up), and voxelwise TBSS is available as a whole-brain sensitivity analysis.

Interpretation

White-matter connectivity (106/106 sessions, n=102 per edge) shows a small, focused set of effects: cerebellum–visual and cerebellum–default-mode coupling (Buckner-7: Cb-Default–Cb-Vis q=0.001, Cb-Default–Cb-DorsAttn q=0.012) and cerebellum–dorsal-attention coupling (King-10: Cb-8/Cb-7–DorsAttn q=0.007/0.013, plus Cb-1–Cont q=0.013 and a cerebellum-internal Cb-3–Cb-7 edge q=0.019). The single-node representation shows only one cortical–subcortical edge (SalVentAttn–Subcortical q=0.020) — the cerebellum-related effects are between cerebellar subregions and specific cortical networks, i.e. the same fine-grained, network-specific pattern the EC analyses show. No limbic→cerebellum SC effect (the strongest EC finding) — consistent with EC reflecting directed dynamics rather than anatomy. All SC effects are cross-sectional group×time changes in streamline density; DWI at 1.7 mm with 6 b0 reverse-PE images gives modest sensitivity, so these are hypothesis-generating.

Methods

Cohort & design

Longitudinal walking intervention, 2 groups (Walking vs Control) × 2 timepoints (pre = ses-01, post = ses-02). All models estimate the group×time interaction (differential change between groups). Mean-FD > 0.3 mm excluded.

Preprocessing

  • fMRIPrep 25.2.5 (MNI152NLin6Asym res-2; no recon-all)
  • XCP-D 26.0.2 — fc variant: aCompCor, FD scrubbing (>0.3mm), bandpass 0.01–0.08 Hz, 6 mm smoothing; ec variant: aCompCor, bandpass 0.01–0.1 Hz, 0 mm smoothing. Confounds regressed at this stage; no re-regression downstream.
  • FastSurfer 2.5.4 for subcortical volumes / cortical thickness

Functional connectivity

442-parcel atlas (Schaefer400 + Tian subcortex + 10 cerebellar). Three separate analysis families: (i) ROI-to-ROI — 442×442 Fisher-z matrices (97,461 edges, NBS), 489-test metric tournament, and block-level metrics across every cerebellum map × estimator (Pearson/Spearman/partial on the block-mean timeseries; LMM ~ group×time + Age + Gender + mean_fd + (1|subject)); (ii) seed-to-brain — region-level seed→network / seed→whole-brain metrics (corrected cohort, LMM/FDR) plus 10-seed voxelwise seed-to-voxel maps (corrected-cohort TFCE re-run, null; Seed-to-Brain tab); (iii) whole-brain voxelwise (ALFF/ReHo, Whole-brain tab). The block-level division comparison uses the ec-variant block timeseries (shared with EC) for comparability; the 442-parcel metric tournament uses the fc variant.

Effective connectivity

Block timeseries are built by script/build_block_timeseries.py. Primary representation — DiFuMo-512 whole-brain: script/annotate_difumo512_yeo7.py assigns every DiFuMo-512 component to cortex/subcortex/cerebellum and to a Yeo-7 network (cortex: Yeo-17→7 dictionary mapping or ≥25% Schaefer-parcel overlap; cerebellum: majority Buckner-2011 overlap; subcortex: dictionary label where present, otherwise dominant group-mean FC with the seven cortical blocks — a fixed, outcome-independent label with subject-bootstrap stability reported in shared/difumo512_annotation_qc.json). Blocks (Ctx-*, Sub-*, Cb-*) are voxel-level BOLD means over the component masks. Sensitivity representations keep the 7 Yeo cortical networks + Subcortical fixed (442-parcel timeseries) and vary only the cerebellum: 1 node (9 nodes; 72 directed edges), functional zones (11 nodes; 110 edges), Buckner-7 (15 nodes; 210 edges), fine DiFuMo-512 cerebellar components (52 nodes; 2,652 edges). King-10 (306 edges) and MDTB-32 (1,560 edges) were also computed and are retained on disk for the publication stage. Every method is run on every representation (method × map matrix): VAR(1) A-matrix (multivariate linear, OLS), rDCM (regression dynamic causal modelling, TAPAS/Julia, Wiener stochastic input, 16 samples/TR, run on HPC), pairwise Granger (bivariate F-statistic), KSG transfer entropy (kNN, k=4) plus a binned plug-in TE. Edge-wise LMM (value ~ group×time + Age + Gender + mean_fd + (1|subject), mean-FD > 0.3 mm excluded) + BH-FDR within map×method; NBS cluster correction applied per representation (all null). All are HRF-latency confounded at TR=0.8 s → hypothesis-generating.

Outlier screen

For every FDR-significant feature in every family (FC metrics, EC edges — including the DiFuMo-512 whole-brain division — SC pairs and DTI/DKI ROI metrics), per-subject post−pre deltas were z-scored within group and |z|>3 flagged; the LMM was refit without flagged subjects (script/outlier_check.py; outputs shared/outlier_flags.csv, shared/outlier_robustness.csv). Structural outliers were screened separately (sub-063 hippocampal loss + ICV instability, sub-077 amygdala loss, sub-067 age-consistent MTL atrophy, sub-099 large ICV, sub-093 borderline putamen — all retained; see the Structural tab outlier screen for the robustness refits).

Voxelwise / seed-to-voxel

ALFF/ReHo (voxelwise), seed-to-voxel Pearson→Fisher-z. Per-subject delta (post−pre) maps; two-sample t-test via FSL randomise, TFCE, 5000 permutations. Cluster composition via FSL atlasq + AAL3v1 (covers cortex, subcortex and cerebellum).

Corrections & caveats

  • BIDS correction (2026-09-25): 6 sessions re-converted from DICOM (sub-034/065/074/084/091 ses-02, sub-089 ses-01); sub-056/057 excluded (ses-02 not their own scans). FastSurfer, fMRIPrep, XCP-D and all downstream FC/EC features were re-run on the corrected data. The first re-extraction attempt silently failed (process-pool OOM); it was re-run serially and verified before the analyses in this report.
  • BH-FDR within families; NBS cluster-level FWER (5,000 perms) for full ROI-to-ROI (FC) and all EC divisions; TFCE for voxelwise.
  • Derived atlas labels: DiFuMo-512 cerebellar components are assigned to Yeo-7 networks by majority Buckner-2011 overlap; subcortical components by dictionary label where present, otherwise by dominant group-mean FC with the cortical blocks (fixed, outcome-independent, bootstrap-stability reported). Results are additionally shown for the published Buckner-7 / zone representations and for the fine cerebellar DiFuMo-512 components so no claim rests on the derived labels alone.
  • Structural connectivity complete (106/106 sessions): 3 re-run sessions used SyN-SDC instead of TOPUP where the b0 reverse-PE pair failed geometry QC (documented caveat); sub-063 was repaired via its FastSurfer surface re-run. SC atlases cover 1-node / King-10 / Buckner-7 / zones; a DiFuMo-512 whole-brain SC build is a publication-stage follow-up.
  • LMM fitted with BFGS (L-BFGS produced singular-Hessian failures on a subset of edges, silently dropping tests).
  • Outlier screen (|z|>3 delta) applied to all significant features; fragile effects are flagged in the tabs.
  • Preliminary — no permutation max-T at the summary level, no split-half replication.
  • EC results non-causal; spectral DCM (SPM) would be the confirmatory step.
